title: Cache exchange rates for 15 minutes
pr_body: The provider rate-limits us; cache rates in-process with a 15 minute TTL.

files.after:
"""Small in-process cache for exchange rates fetched from the provider."""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from app.rates_client import fetch_rate

RATE_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Entry:
    rate: float
    fetched_at: datetime


_cache: dict[tuple[str, str], _Entry] = {}
_lock = threading.Lock()


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


def get_rate(base: str, quote: str) -> float:
    """Return the base->quote rate, refreshing it at most every RATE_TTL_SECONDS."""
    key = (base.upper(), quote.upper())
    with _lock:
        entry = _cache.get(key)
        if entry is not None and (_now() - entry.fetched_at).seconds < RATE_TTL_SECONDS:
            return entry.rate
    rate = fetch_rate(*key)
    with _lock:
        _cache[key] = _Entry(rate=rate, fetched_at=_now())
    return rate


def clear() -> None:
    with _lock:
        _cache.clear()

bugs.title: timedelta.seconds ignores days
bugs.rationale: timedelta.seconds is only the seconds component (0-86399), not the total. An entry fetched 1 day and 5 minutes ago has .seconds == 300 and is served as fresh, so stale exchange rates are returned for the first 15 minutes of every following day.

acceptable.rationale: Concurrent misses fetch the same rate twice (thundering herd); minor.
